language_wrapper: Inside a fixed regular {num_sides}-gon, consider all straight segments that connect pairs of its vertices (i.e., its sides and diagonals). A rectangle is valid if each side of the rectangle lies entirely on one of these segments and the rectangle lies completely inside the polygon. How many such rectangles exist if exactly {edge_count} of the rectangle's sides coincide with sides of the polygon (the other sides, if any, are diagonals)?
hardness_rationale: The family preserves the core idea (counting rectangles formed by chords of a regular polygon) but adds a global constraint: exactly 0 or 2 sides must coincide with polygon sides. This forces careful case management beyond the seed's unconstrained count and eliminates many symmetric shortcuts. The solver must understand the parallel/perpendicular line classes induced by chords, control segment-length constraints (intersections must lie within finite chord segments), and handle edge-type versus diagonal-type lines simultaneously. With n chosen from larger, divisible-by-4 values (>=12), the combinatorics and geometry both scale, making it at least as hard as the seed problem.
notes: Implementation counts rectangles by brute-force segment intersection with tolerance to avoid floating errors; using orientation classes (i+j mod n) leverages the midpoint-tangent characterization of chord directions. The wrap-around side (n-1,0) is added explicitly to include all n sides.
source_question: Find the number of rectangles that can be formed inside a fixed regular dodecagon ( $12$ -gon) where each side of the rectangle lies on either a side or a diagonal of the dodecagon. The diagram below shows three of those rectangles. [asy] unitsize(0.6 inch); for(int i=0; i<360; i+=30) { dot(dir(i), 4+black); draw(dir(i)--dir(i+30)); } draw(dir(120)--dir(330)); filldraw(dir(210)--dir(240)--dir(30)--dir(60)--cycle, mediumgray, linewidth(1.5)); draw((0,0.366)--(0.366,0), linewidth(1.5)); [/asy]
